# Mechanics

| name | summary |
|---|---|
| [Adaptive threat scaling](adaptive-threat-scaling.md) | Threat intensity is computed from a measure of the player's strength, such as wealth, population, time survived, or recent performance. |
| [Adjacency scoring](adjacency-scoring.md) | A placement's value is computed from a table of bonuses and penalties for the placements around it. |
| [Advertising and awareness](advertising-awareness.md) | Spending on advertising raises a demand or awareness stock that decays without upkeep and scales how many customers arrive or buy. |
| [Advisors](advisors.md) | In-world advisor characters monitor simulation indicators, summarize problems, and recommend actions. |
| [Agent inspection](agent-inspection.md) | Selecting an agent opens a panel that reveals its needs, mood contributors, current job, and the reasons behind its behavior. |
| [Agent pathfinding](agent-pathfinding.md) | Agents compute routes through space using movement costs, and the routes they choose shape congestion, travel time, and access. |
| [Agent skills](agent-skills.md) | Agents gain skill through practice or training, and skill sets work speed, quality, and access to tasks. |
| [Alerts feed](alerts-feed.md) | A notification layer surfaces discrete events and threshold crossings with severity and a link to their location. |
| [Animal husbandry](animal-husbandry.md) | Domestic animals are housed, fed, tended, and bred, and they yield products whose quantity and quality depend on their care. |
| [Aspirations and wants](aspiration-wants.md) | An agent's long-term aspiration and current state generate short-horizon wants, and sometimes fears, whose fulfillment pays into a reward meter or currency. |
| [Asynchronous shared regions](async-shared-region.md) | Separate players' simulations affect each other asynchronously through shared regions, visits, or exchanges of goods and services. |
| [Attribute-driven match engine](attribute-match-engine.md) | Contest outcomes are simulated play by play from participant attributes, tactics, and randomness instead of being played directly. |
| [Auctions](auctions.md) | Goods, land, or rights are allocated by bidding procedures in which players or agents compete on price under rules for timing, ties, and reserves. |
| [Autonomy levels](autonomy-levels.md) | The degree to which agents act on their own is adjustable, from full free will to explicit commands only. |
| [Blueprints](blueprints.md) | Player-made layouts can be saved, stamped as build orders, copied, and shared as text or files. |
| [Board confidence](board-confidence.md) | An evaluator such as a board, owner, or chairman sets expectations, updates a confidence stock from results against them, and fires the player below a threshold. |
| [Building placement](free-placement.md) | The player places discrete structures on a grid or freely, and placement constraints turn layout into a spatial puzzle. |
| [Byproducts and waste](byproducts-waste.md) | Production emits secondary outputs such as sludge, garbage, heat, or spent fuel that must be handled or they impair the system. |
| [Care-dependent development](care-dependent-development.md) | A creature's or character's accumulated care or attribute history selects which form or outcome it develops into at each stage boundary, from a fixed branching table. |
| [Career ladder](career-ladder.md) | Characters advance through ranked job levels by meeting skill, relationship, and performance requirements. |
| [Causal breakdown tooltips](causal-tooltips.md) | Hovering a derived value shows the named modifiers that produce it, and terms inside the tooltip can be hovered in turn. |
| [Citizen satisfaction](citizen-satisfaction.md) | An aggregate satisfaction score computed from services, conditions, and events modulates growth, productivity, and unrest. |
| [Collection goals](collection-goals.md) | Catalogs of items, species, or bundles give the player sets to complete for rewards or recognition. |
| [Combination discovery](combination-discovery.md) | The player combines owned elements to discover the products of a hidden recipe graph, and finding recipes is itself the goal. |
| [Comparative histograms](comparative-histograms.md) | A player's solution is plotted against distributions of other players' scores on several metrics. |
| [Contagion](contagion.md) | Disease spreads between agents or regions via contact rates and moves hosts through compartments such as susceptible, infected, and recovered. |
| [Content sharing](content-sharing.md) | Player creations such as buildings, creatures, or blueprints are uploaded, browsed, rated, and imported into other players' games. |
| [Contracts and orders](contracts-orders.md) | Discrete jobs with requirements, deadlines, and payouts, such as deliveries or commissions, drive income and planning. |
| [Conveyor transport](conveyor-transport.md) | Items move continuously on belts or lanes with throughput limits, splitters, merges, and priorities. |
| [Corruption leakage](corruption-leakage.md) | A corruption level driven by spending, administrative reach, or size removes a share of revenue or output until countermeasures bring it down. |
| [Creature care](creature-care.md) | The player directly feeds, cleans, and plays with a creature whose needs decay; neglect causes sickness, stunted growth, or death. |
| [Creature learning](creature-learning.md) | A creature's behavior is learned from player reward and punishment or from neural adaptation over its life. |
| [Crime and policing](crime-policing.md) | Crime levels arise from local conditions such as land value, density, or unemployment, and police coverage, prisons, and justice reduce them. |
| [Crisis countdown](crisis-countdown.md) | A known future crisis such as a storm, winter, cure, or deadline is announced in advance, and the remaining time structures preparation. |
| [Crop cultivation](crop-cultivation.md) | Planted crops progress through growth stages over days or seasons depending on water, soil, and season, then are harvested. |
| [Crowd preferences](crowd-preferences.md) | Large visitor populations with individual preferences, budgets, and tolerances choose attractions and react with visible thoughts. |
| [Culture and religion conversion](culture-religion-conversion.md) | Provinces or population groups carry culture and faith identities that drift or are converted by missionaries, policies, and rulers, changing unrest, opinion, and bonuses. |
| [Customer value choice](customer-value-choice.md) | Customers choose among offerings by comparing price to perceived value and personal preference. |
| [Daily action budget](daily-action-budget.md) | A per-day pool of energy, stamina, or time slots limits how many actions the player can take, and the day's end resets it and forces prioritization. |
| [Daily schedules](daily-schedules.md) | Agents follow time-blocked routines for work, sleep, and leisure that create rhythms of demand across the day. |
| [Data overlays](data-overlays.md) | Map layers visualize hidden variables such as land value, pollution, coverage, or traffic. |
| [Dated technology timeline](dated-tech-timeline.md) | New vehicle models, platforms, or products enter and leave availability on a calendar tied to in-game dates rather than to research, forcing fleet or platform renewal. |
| [Day-night cycle](day-night-cycle.md) | A diurnal cycle changes light, visibility, temperature, and which agents are active, so activity follows the hour of the day. |
| [Decoration and beauty](decoration-beauty.md) | Decorative objects and scenery carry beauty values that are aggregated over tiles, rooms, or radii and feed agent mood or ratings. |
| [Delegation to AI managers](delegation-to-ai.md) | Subsystems are handed to AI managers or governors that pursue player-set goals within bounds. |
| [Delivery-time payment](delivery-time-payment.md) | Payment for a delivery depends on cargo type, quantity, distance, and transit time, with each cargo losing value at its own rate the longer it travels. |
| [Deposit depletion](deposit-depletion.md) | Extractable deposits hold finite quantities and run out, forcing expansion, relocation, or substitution. |
| [Design performance rating](design-performance-rating.md) | Player-built designs are run or analyzed and scored on simulated metrics such as ride excitement, bridge stress, or cost and cycles. |
| [Designation orders](designation-orders.md) | The player marks tiles or objects for work such as dig, chop, or build, and autonomous agents claim and execute the jobs. |
| [Diagnose and repair](diagnose-repair.md) | The player inspects a machine, finds faulty parts with tools and tests, disassembles in order to reach them, and repairs or replaces them. |
| [Diagnosis and treatment](diagnosis-treatment.md) | Patients present symptoms, examinations reduce uncertainty about a hidden condition, and the correct treatment cures it while wrong or late treatment harms. |
| [Dilemma cards](dilemma-cards.md) | Discrete choice events present a situation with a few options that each shift meters, values, or flags in tradeoff. |
| [Direct avatar control](direct-avatar.md) | The player directly controls one embodied character's movement and actions in the simulated world. |
| [Dynasty succession](dynasty-succession.md) | When the player character dies, play continues as an heir chosen by inheritance rules. |
| [Education and workforce](education-workforce.md) | Education levels gate job types, and schooling converts the labor pool into higher levels over time. |
| [Elections](elections.md) | Periodic votes by simulated or real voters determine tenure or policy. |
| [Embodied skill control](embodied-skill-control.md) | Real-time motor skill operating a simulated mechanism, such as hand-flying, driving, or surgery, is the main challenge. |
| [Equity and buyouts](equity-buyouts.md) | Companies issue shares whose price tracks performance, and players buy them for profit or accumulate a majority to take control of rivals. |
| [Execution budget](execution-budget.md) | Player-written programs are metered against a simulated compute budget, such as CPU per tick, tick cost per operation, instruction slots, or RAM, which makes efficiency the scarce resource. |
| [Faction diplomacy](faction-diplomacy.md) | Factions hold relations with each other, and treaties, alliances, and wars follow from interests and opinion. |
| [Falling-sand materials](falling-sand-materials.md) | Every pixel or cell holds a material whose class rule makes it fall, flow, or rise by swapping with neighbors, with reactions layered on top. |
| [Fire spread](fire-spread.md) | Fire ignites and spreads across flammable cells or objects at rates set by fuel, wind, and moisture, consuming what it burns. |
| [Flight aerodynamics](flight-aerodynamics.md) | Lift, drag, thrust, and control-surface forces computed from airspeed and attitude govern aircraft motion. |
| [Fluid and gas simulation](fluid-gas-simulation.md) | Liquids and gases stored per cell or as fields flow, mix, and pressurize across space according to pressure and density differences. |
| [Fluid pipe networks](fluid-pipe-network.md) | Fluids such as water, oil, sewage, or gas flow through pipes with pressure or throughput limits between producers and consumers. |
| [Fog of war](fog-of-war.md) | Parts of the world stay hidden or stale until observed by the player's units, structures, or sensors. |
| [Food web](food-web.md) | Species eat and are eaten along a feeding graph, so populations rise, crash, and oscillate under predator-prey dynamics. |
| [Forecasting](forecasting.md) | The interface projects future states such as resource runway, budget balance, or upcoming weather. |
| [Generative content on demand](generative-content.md) | A generative model creates new content such as text, items, recipes, or rules at runtime in response to player input. |
| [God powers](god-powers.md) | The player spends a power resource on miracles that alter terrain, weather, or creatures. |
| [Goods consumption](goods-consumption.md) | A population consumes goods at per-capita rates; unmet consumption lowers satisfaction or blocks advancement. |
| [Gossip propagation](gossip-propagation.md) | Information about events spreads through social contacts, changing what agents know and believe. |
| [Habitat suitability](habitat-suitability.md) | Species or crops thrive only where conditions such as terrain, temperature, water, and cover match their needs, scored per location. |
| [Hand crafting](hand-crafting.md) | The player or avatar combines carried components into items from a recipe list, gated by workstations and known recipes. |
| [Hauling jobs](hauling-jobs.md) | Agents pick up and carry items between locations via a job queue, making hauling capacity a hidden throughput constraint. |
| [Heat transfer](heat-transfer.md) | Temperature diffuses between cells, materials, and objects by conductivity and heat capacity, and thresholds trigger phase changes and damage. |
| [History chronicle](history-chronicle.md) | The game records significant simulation events into a structured history that players can browse and other systems can reference. |
| [Hydrology](hydrology.md) | Water flows across terrain and through rivers by height differences, producing floods, droughts, irrigation, and dam management. |
| [Immigration by attractiveness](immigration-attractiveness.md) | Population arrives or leaves based on attractiveness such as jobs, housing, and happiness relative to alternatives. |
| [Injury body model](injury-body-model.md) | Bodies are hierarchies of parts with their own damage, and wounds, bleeding, infection, and prosthetics change capacities such as moving and manipulation. |
| [Interest groups](interest-groups.md) | Factions within a polity have clout and preferences over policies, and their approval gates what the player can do. |
| [Labor market](labor-market.md) | Workers fill jobs by type and education; mismatches create unemployment or labor shortages that throttle production. |
| [Land value](land-value.md) | Each location's value is computed from nearby amenities, nuisances, and access, and it drives density and building upgrades. |
| [Lifecycle and aging](lifecycle-aging.md) | Agents are born, age through life stages with different capabilities, and die. |
| [Loans and debt](loans-debt.md) | Capital can be borrowed at interest with repayment schedules, so leverage accelerates both growth and failure. |
| [Loss on death](loss-on-death.md) | When a character or ship is destroyed, its carried or fitted assets are lost or dropped at the death site for the owner or others to recover, with insurance or retrieval rules as softeners. |
| [Machine boosting](machine-boosting.md) | Per-machine modifiers such as modules, beacons, clock speed, or coatings trade extra power, scarce items, or currency for faster or more productive machines. |
| [Material interactions](material-interactions.md) | A rule table defines how elements such as fire, water, and electricity change materials and each other on contact. |
| [Megaproject sink](megaproject-sink.md) | A terminal construction absorbs very large quantities of produced goods in staged phases and serves as the long-run goal and output sink of a production game. |
| [Memories and thoughts](memories-thoughts.md) | Events create itemized, time-limited mood modifiers or lasting memories that shape later behavior. |
| [Milestone unlocks](milestone-unlocks.md) | Reaching thresholds such as population, output, or score unlocks new buildings, areas, or features. |
| [Military operations](military-operations.md) | Units with modeled sensors, weapons, platforms, and doctrine conduct operations at operational fidelity, mostly under player orders and automated behavior. |
| [Modding API](modding-api.md) | Official hooks for scripts and data definitions let players change and extend the simulation's content and rules. |
| [Modular assembly](modular-assembly.md) | The player builds machines, vehicles, or creatures from parts whose stats and physical arrangement determine how the result behaves. |
| [Mood and breakdowns](mood-breakdown.md) | Mood aggregates needs, memories, and environment, and crossing thresholds triggers mental breaks or inspired performance. |
| [Natural selection](natural-selection.md) | Differential survival and reproduction by fitness shifts trait distributions across generations. |
| [Natural-language interaction](natural-language-interaction.md) | The player communicates with characters by free text or voice, and the system interprets intent and responds. |
| [Needs decay](needs-decay.md) | Each agent has needs such as hunger, energy, social, and fun that decay over time and are restored by actions. |
| [Negotiation](negotiation.md) | The player and an AI party exchange offers and counteroffers over wages, prices, or contract terms against the AI's hidden reservation value until a deal is struck or talks fail. |
| [Off-screen life progression](offscreen-life-progression.md) | Households or agents outside the player's active simulation advance through life events on a cheap stochastic model, so the world changes between visits. |
| [Opinion modifiers](opinion-modifiers.md) | Opinions are sums of named, decaying modifiers from events and traits, itemized for the player. |
| [Orbital mechanics](orbital-mechanics.md) | Bodies move under gravity, and maneuvers spend delta-v to change orbits, intercepts, and transfers. |
| [Pause and speed control](variable-speed.md) | The player pauses the simulation and switches between speed multipliers, trading attention against elapsed game time. |
| [Periodic ticks](periodic-ticks.md) | Some state changes, such as budgets, harvests, or growth, resolve in batches at fixed intervals like a month or a year rather than continuously. |
| [Permadeath](permadeath.md) | Death of agents or the avatar is permanent, and the save system prevents undoing it. |
| [Persistent shared world](persistent-world.md) | A server-side world keeps running and keeps its state for many players, whether or not any one player is logged in. |
| [Personality traits](personality-traits.md) | Fixed or slow-changing traits change each agent's needs, preferences, and available actions. |
| [Planetary climate](planetary-climate.md) | Planet-scale variables such as atmospheric composition, temperature, sea level, and biosphere evolve under coupled feedbacks and can be deliberately altered. |
| [Player legislation](player-legislation.md) | Players author, propose, and vote on rules that the game then enforces inside a shared world, such as taxes, bans, and permits. |
| [Player organizations](player-organizations.md) | Players form corporations, guilds, or governments with membership, roles, permissions, and shared assets. |
| [Player programming](player-programming.md) | The player writes code in a language the game executes to control units, machines, or the world. |
| [Player-driven markets](player-driven-market.md) | Players post buy and sell orders in shared order books, and prices emerge from player behavior. |
| [Policy influence network](policy-influence-network.md) | Policies, indicators, and voter groups connect through a weighted causal graph with delays. |
| [Policy toggles](policy-toggles.md) | Enactable laws or policies change simulation rules with explicit tradeoffs. |
| [Political capital](political-capital.md) | An abstract governing currency accrues each period from leaders, factions, or population welfare and is spent on policy changes, edicts, and other state actions. |
| [Pollution spread](pollution-spread.md) | Pollution emitted by sources accumulates and diffuses across land, water, or air cells and harms health, land value, or growth, or provokes threats. |
| [Population strata](population-strata.md) | The population is divided into classes or tiers with distinct needs, roles, and upgrade paths. |
| [Power allocation](power-allocation.md) | The player splits a fixed power budget among a vehicle's subsystems in real time, trading shields, weapons, engines, and life support against each other. |
| [Power grid](power-grid.md) | Generators produce energy that is distributed over a connected network to consumers; shortfalls cause brownouts or shutdowns. |
| [Procedural build assist](procedural-build-assist.md) | Coarse player input such as a block or a drawn wall is turned into detailed, organic structures by procedural rules. |
| [Procedural characters](procedural-characters.md) | Characters are generated with names, backstories, traits, skills, and appearance sampled from constrained tables or grammars. |
| [Procedural checklists](procedural-checklists.md) | Operating simulated equipment requires performing ordered steps on modeled controls that mirror real procedures, with system states gating each step. |
| [Procedural terrain](procedural-terrain.md) | Maps are generated from a seed through noise, erosion, climate, and placement rules. |
| [Product development](product-development.md) | The player configures a product's features, and a simulated market scores it against trends, quality, and competition. |
| [Production chains](production-chain.md) | Buildings or machines convert input goods into output goods via fixed recipes and cycle times, forming multi-step dependency trees. |
| [Programming by demonstration](programming-by-demonstration.md) | An agent or vehicle learns a routine by recording the player performing it, and the recording becomes a replayable, sometimes editable, program. |
| [Projectile ballistics](projectile-ballistics.md) | Shots are simulated as projectiles in flight with velocity, gravity, drag, and penetration, so range, angle, and lead decide hits rather than an instant trace or a dice roll. |
| [Public transit lines](public-transit.md) | Player-drawn lines with stops and vehicles carry passengers whose ridership depends on coverage, frequency, and transfers. |
| [PvP security zones](pvp-security-zones.md) | A shared world is divided into zones whose rules set whether players may attack each other and what an aggressor pays, such as NPC police response or lost standing. |
| [Quality tiers](quality-tiers.md) | Produced items carry quality grades derived from inputs, worker skill, or chance, scaling their value or effect. |
| [Raid defense](raid-defense.md) | Settlements defend against periodic attacks with walls, turrets, traps, and fighters placed and commanded by the player. |
| [Rail signaling](rail-signaling.md) | Block and path signals partition track so trains can share it without collision; throughput depends on signal design. |
| [Random disasters](random-disasters.md) | Stochastic disasters such as fires, floods, earthquakes, storms, or meteors strike at random times and places and damage the system. |
| [RCI demand](rci-demand.md) | A demand signal for residential, commercial, and industrial land derived from the balance of jobs, workers, and goods. |
| [Real-time clock](real-time-clock.md) | Game time follows the real-world clock and calendar, so the world advances, ages, and holds events while the game is closed. |
| [Real-world data feeds](real-world-data-feeds.md) | Simulation state is initialized or driven at runtime by external real-world data such as map imagery, elevation, star catalogs, live weather, or live traffic instead of authored or procedural content. |
| [Relationship values](relationship-values.md) | Pairwise numeric affinity between characters changes with interactions and drives social choices. |
| [Renewable regrowth](renewable-regrowth.md) | Harvested stocks such as forests, fish, game, and soil regenerate over time at density-dependent rates, allowing sustainable yield or overexploitation. |
| [Reputation](reputation.md) | A standing value with a faction or the public changes access, prices, and how others respond. |
| [Request-provider logistics](request-provider-logistics.md) | Containers declare per-item requests and supplies, and a dispatcher sends drones or robots from providers to requesters without fixed routes. |
| [Resource extraction](resource-extraction.md) | Workers or machines harvest raw materials from map nodes (ore, trees, fish, oil) at rates set by tools, labor, and node richness. |
| [Rigid-body physics](rigid-body-physics.md) | Objects with mass and inertia move under forces and collide, constrained by contacts and joints solved each step. |
| [Rival firms](rival-firms.md) | AI or player competitors contest markets, prices, and assets; market share decides who wins. |
| [Road networks](road-network.md) | Roads and paths define connectivity; buildings must connect to function, and travel cost depends on network geometry. |
| [Romance and family](romance-family.md) | Agents court, partner, marry, and form families according to compatibility and relationship state. |
| [Room recognition](room-recognition.md) | Enclosed spaces are detected by flood fill and classified into room types by their size and contents, and the type grants effects. |
| [Rule-checking inspection](rule-checking-inspection.md) | The player checks documents, people, or cargo against a rulebook that changes over time, under time pressure, with penalties for errors. |
| [Scenario objectives](scenario-objectives.md) | Preset maps or situations come with explicit goals, constraints, and often a deadline. |
| [Scouting knowledge](scouting-knowledge.md) | Entity attributes are known only with uncertainty that scouting effort reduces. |
| [Seasonal world reset](seasonal-world-reset.md) | A shared world runs for a bounded season and is then wiped and restarted, often with rule changes carried into the next season. |
| [Seasons](seasons.md) | A seasonal calendar cycles conditions such as temperature, daylight, and growing windows that govern growth, demand, and risk. |
| [Service coverage](service-coverage.md) | Service buildings such as police, fire, clinics, and schools satisfy demand within a radius or network distance, up to a capacity. |
| [Service queues](service-queues.md) | Agents wait in lines for limited-capacity services; waiting time feeds back into satisfaction and throughput. |
| [Signal circuits](signal-circuits.md) | In-world wires, sensors, and logic elements carry signals that read machine state and control machines. |
| [Simulated history generation](history-generation.md) | World generation simulates years to centuries of civilizations, figures, and events before play begins, producing the starting world. |
| [Smart objects](smart-objects.md) | Objects advertise the need satisfaction they offer, and agents query nearby objects to decide what to do. |
| [Social exchanges](social-exchanges.md) | Discrete social moves such as flirt, insult, or apologize have preconditions on social state and norms, and they update relationships. |
| [Soft-body deformation](soft-body-deformation.md) | Objects built from mass nodes and spring beams bend, crumple, and break under stress, and deformation persists. |
| [Spoilage](spoilage.md) | Perishable goods lose value or rot over time depending on storage conditions such as temperature and containers. |
| [Stability and unrest](stability-unrest.md) | Grievances accumulate into unrest that triggers protests, strikes, or revolt. |
| [Staff hiring and rosters](staff-hiring.md) | The player hires individual staff with skills, traits, and wages to operate a facility or team. |
| [Statistical combat resolution](stat-combat-resolution.md) | Battles between units resolve from attack, defense, morale, terrain, and random rolls in rounds rather than from physics or modeled sensors and weapons. |
| [Stats dashboards](stats-dashboards.md) | Graphs and tables show the recorded history of simulation variables over selectable time windows. |
| [Stimulus attraction](stimulus-attraction.md) | Player actions emit sound or light stimuli with a radius and decay, and agents that perceive them move toward the source, so managing emissions is part of survival. |
| [Storage and buffers](storage-capacity.md) | Goods occupy finite storage; buffers decouple producers from consumers, and full storage blocks production. |
| [Storyteller director](storyteller-director.md) | A director AI chooses which events to fire and when, pacing them by a model of tension and the current state. |
| [Stress accumulation](stress-accumulation.md) | A slow per-agent stress stock integrates negative experiences scaled by personality and, as it crosses levels, triggers breaks or lasting changes. |
| [Structural integrity](structural-integrity.md) | Structures carry support values or loads propagated from the ground, and elements that lose support or exceed their limits collapse. |
| [Subsystem damage](subsystem-damage.md) | A vehicle or ship is a set of named components with their own integrity, and damage to one removes its capacity, such as power, thrust, shields, or sensors, until it is repaired. |
| [Supply lines](supply-lines.md) | Remote units or outposts need a continuous connection to a supply source; cutting the connection causes attrition. |
| [Supply-demand pricing](supply-demand-pricing.md) | Prices adjust to supply and demand, so scarcity raises prices and gluts lower them. |
| [Surface work tools](surface-work-tools.md) | The player applies a tool to surfaces to clean, paint, or strip them, and a per-surface coverage state shows visible progress toward completion. |
| [Survival meters](survival-meters.md) | The avatar's bodily stocks such as hunger, thirst, warmth, and fatigue deplete over time and, if unmanaged, drain health and kill. |
| [Taxation](taxation.md) | Player-set tax rates convert economic activity into revenue at the cost of growth, happiness, or competitiveness. |
| [Tech tree](tech-tree.md) | A research or unlock graph gates buildings, recipes, or abilities behind prerequisites and accumulated research. |
| [Terraforming](terraforming.md) | The player raises, lowers, flattens, or repaints terrain, usually at a cost, to make land usable or to reshape water and paths. |
| [Terrain deformation](terrain-deformation.md) | Wheels, feet, and impacts displace soft ground such as mud and snow, and the persistent ruts change traction for later passes. |
| [Territorial control](territorial-control.md) | Map regions have an owner and a current controller; occupation flips control in war, and peace, purchase, or integration transfers ownership at a cost in time, unrest, or political currency. |
| [Track laying](track-laying.md) | The player builds rail or coaster track segment by segment under grade, curvature, terrain, and cost constraints, and vehicles then run on the resulting path. |
| [Trade routes](trade-routes.md) | Goods are exchanged between settlements, regions, or foreign markets along routes with price differences, tariffs, and transit time. |
| [Traffic congestion](traffic-congestion.md) | Trips route over a capacitated network; volume beyond capacity raises travel time and delays services and deliveries. |
| [Trait inheritance](trait-inheritance.md) | Offspring inherit traits or genes from their parents with recombination, variation, or mutation. |
| [Travel mode choice](travel-mode-choice.md) | Agents choose among walking, cycling, driving, and transit for each trip by comparing time, money, and comfort costs, which sets how demand splits across networks. |
| [Treasury and budget](budget-treasury.md) | A money stock with income and expense flows such as taxes, upkeep, wages, and service funding; a negative balance leads to debt or failure. |
| [Triggered event chains](triggered-event-chains.md) | Authored event templates fire when state conditions hold, and their outcomes schedule follow-up events that chain into multi-step stories. |
| [Turn structure](turn-structure.md) | The simulation advances in discrete turns, each divided into ordered phases in which players decide and the world then resolves. |
| [Unit commands](unit-commands.md) | The player issues direct orders to specific units or agents, overriding their autonomous behavior. |
| [Utility action selection](utility-action-selection.md) | Agents choose actions by scoring options against needs and context, then picking the highest or sampling among high scores. |
| [Vehicle dynamics](vehicle-dynamics.md) | Tire, suspension, drivetrain, and weight-transfer models compute vehicle handling from forces at each wheel. |
| [Vehicle routes and schedules](vehicle-route-scheduling.md) | Vehicles are assigned ordered stops with load and unload rules to move goods or passengers between nodes. |
| [Vertical layers](vertical-layers.md) | The world has stacked layers such as z-levels, floors, or underground networks, and rules connect what happens between them. |
| [Villager requests](villager-requests.md) | Characters generate small requests or quests from templates whose parameters are filled from simulation state, with rewards and deadlines. |
| [Voxel destruction](voxel-destruction.md) | The world is built from small destructible units that can be removed, broken loose, and burned anywhere. |
| [Walker service delivery](walker-service-delivery.md) | Services are delivered by agents walking routes from their building, so coverage depends on where walkers actually go. |
| [War score and peace terms](war-score-peace.md) | Each war tracks a score or exhaustion level from battles, occupation, and war goals, and that value caps what a peace settlement can demand or forces capitulation. |
| [Wear and breakdown](wear-breakdown.md) | Assets lose condition with use and age, breakdown risk rises as condition falls, and maintenance or repair restores it. |
| [Weather](weather.md) | Weather states such as rain, storms, snow, wind, and temperature change over time and modify activities and other systems. |
| [Work priorities](work-priorities.md) | The player sets which agents do which job types in what order, and agents self-assign from that priority table. |
| [Zoning](zoning.md) | The player paints land-use zones, and the simulation decides whether and what to build, upgrade, or abandon on each zoned lot. |
